preamble: Kawasaki Disease  |  100-Point Adverse Prognostic Score  |  AHA 2017 KD Guidelines / JCS 2020 KD Guidelines / AHA 2022 CAA Risk Classification  |  Long-term Coronary Artery Aneurysm and Ischemia Risk  |  Progression Trajectory: Fast / Moderate / Slow

questions.question: Is there a giant coronary artery aneurysm (Z-score ≥10 or absolute diameter ≥8 mm) in LAD or RCA?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — giant CAA confirmed (AHA Class V); highest thrombosis, stenosis, and MI risk; dual antiplatelet + anticoagulation mandatory; interventional cardiology and cardiac surgery on team

questions.question: Is there a large coronary artery aneurysm (Z-score 7–9.9 or diameter 6–7.9 mm) in LAD or RCA?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — large CAA confirmed (AHA Class IV); high thrombosis risk; anticoagulation + antiplatelet therapy; stress testing and coronary imaging at 6–12 months

questions.question: Is there a small (Z-score 2.5–4.9) or medium (Z-score 5–6.9) coronary artery aneurysm on echo or CTA?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — small-medium CAA present (AHA Class II–III); antiplatelet therapy; serial echo every 6–12 months; majority of small aneurysms regress within 1–2 years

questions.question: Does coronary CTA or invasive angiography show ≥50% luminal stenosis in LAD, RCA, or LCx?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — obstructive coronary disease confirmed; myocardial ischemia risk; stress perfusion imaging required; revascularization (PCI or CABG) may be indicated

questions.question: Does stress MRI, stress echo, or nuclear perfusion imaging show a fixed or reversible perfusion defect?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — myocardial ischemia or infarct confirmed; revascularization evaluation required; long-term anticoagulation and cardioprotective therapy intensification

questions.question: Did fever persist or recur ≥36 hours after completion of the first IVIG dose (2 g/kg)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — IVIG resistance confirmed; present in ~10–20% of patients; independently associated with higher CAA risk; second IVIG dose, infliximab, or corticosteroids required

questions.question: Was IVIG administered after day 10 of fever, or was diagnosis and treatment significantly delayed?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — late treatment confirmed; CAA formation risk doubles when IVIG given after day 10; coronary surveillance intensification required

questions.question: Is LVEF <50% on echo during acute phase or at follow-up (myocarditis-related dysfunction)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — LV systolic dysfunction from acute myocarditis or ischemic injury; heart failure management + close follow-up; persistent dysfunction at 6 weeks warrants CMR

questions.question: Is there a moderate-to-large pericardial effusion or clinical myocarditis (troponin elevation + LV dysfunction) on presentation?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — significant myopericardial involvement confirmed; associated with more severe inflammatory burden and higher CAA risk; corticosteroid adjunct therapy considered

questions.question: Is platelet count >1,000,000/mm³ (extreme thrombocytosis) in the subacute phase (days 7–21)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — extreme thrombocytosis confirmed; highest platelet-mediated thrombosis risk within aneurysms; antiplatelet therapy intensification; avoid aspirin discontinuation

questions.question: Was the patient younger than 6 months at time of Kawasaki diagnosis?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — infants <6 months have highest CAA risk, most atypical presentation, and highest IVIG resistance rates; heightened surveillance protocol required

questions.question: Has the patient had a second confirmed episode of Kawasaki disease?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — recurrent KD confirmed; ~1–3% recurrence rate; each episode carries independent CAA risk; lifelong cardiology follow-up mandatory

questions.question: Has the patient been lost to cardiology follow-up for >2 years with known CAA history?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — follow-up gap with known aneurysm history; coronary CTA or invasive angiography required to establish current anatomy; risk of undetected stenosis or thrombosis
